LESSON: MUSICAL

Grade: PP2
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PERFORMANCE
Topic 9.1: Musical

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Musical. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What rhyme did you recite?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform simple rhymes for with each other during play entertainment to enhance social play
2. recite a range of musical • Guide learners to sing and rhymes to enhance perform actions rhymes creativity e.g. Baa baa black sheep

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MUSICAL
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Musical helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MUSICAL
Study Musical like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Perform simple rhymes for with each other during play entertainment to enhance social play

What this means
In this part you learn to perform simple rhymes for with each other during play entertainment to enhance social play. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform simple rhymes for with each other during play entertainment to enhance social play.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Musical” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform simple rhymes for with each other during play entertainment to enhance social play. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Recite a range of musical • Guide learners to sing and rhymes to enhance perform actions rhymes creativity e.g. Baa baa black sheep

What this means
In this part you learn to recite a range of musical • Guide learners to sing and rhymes to enhance perform actions rhymes creativity e.g. Baa baa black sheep. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recite a range of musical • Guide learners to sing and rhymes to enhance perform actions rhymes creativity e.g. Baa baa black sheep.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Musical in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recite a range of musical • Guide learners to sing and rhymes to enhance perform actions rhymes creativity e.g. Baa baa black sheep. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Musical is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Musical” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform simple rhymes for with each other during play entertainment to enhance social play)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Musical in your own words. (skill: recite a range of musical • Guide learners to sing and rhymes to enhance perform actions rhymes creativity e.g. Baa baa black sheep)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Musical to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: perform simple rhymes for with each other during play entertainment to enhance social play.
3. Practise this skill: recite a range of musical • Guide learners to sing and rhymes to enhance perform actions rhymes creativity e.g. Baa baa black sheep.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Musical from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Musical: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Musical?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What rhyme did you recite?
2. Which rhyme did you love rhythmic patterns perform simple rhymes most?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Musical means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: perform simple rhymes for with each other during play entertainment to enhance social play.
5. Be able to: recite a range of musical • Guide learners to sing and rhymes to enhance perform actions rhymes creativity e.g. Baa baa black sheep.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
